why: I compared each verifier PASS/FAIL condition with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 3 and 5 test only what their expect lines say: exit 1 with empty stdout; `bad config:`, the exact path and line 3 column 3; `OK` meaning it threw and the message has the path; tests pass at head and a path-asserting test fails at base. Check 4 breaks the criterion. Its PASS needs "the output is exactly the three lines `listening on 9000`, `exit 0`, `{\"port\":9000}`", and its FAIL covers "a different stdout line". Expect line 4 only requires exit 0, that stdout includes `listening on 9000`, and that loadConfig returns `{ port: 9000 }`. It does not rule out other output. Stderr is also not redirected in that command, so a harmless Node warning would fail the check. Demanding exact output is stricter than the words and belongs under Advisory.
